title: Group: legal entity register and organization charts
source_system: Corporate secretary's entity management system; HR organization charts
what_it_shows: Cris Santos Company Holdings, Inc. is an SEC registrant and holding company with three operating subsidiaries (Crude Oil Production, Power Generation, Crude Logistics) and corporate shared services (identity, network, security operations, OT security engineering, cloud and data platform, ERP, HR, finance, legal, internal audit). Headquarters in Florida; operations in Texas, New Mexico, Oklahoma and Florida; no offshore, Outer Continental Shelf, waterfront or MTSA-regulated facility is listed. Organization charts show the Group CISO, the Group OT Security Director reporting to the Group CISO, the Group Chief Risk Officer, the Group General Counsel, the three division security and compliance leads, the Production Vice President of Operations Technology, the Power Generation Vice President of Generation (designated CIP Senior Manager) and NERC Compliance Manager, the Crude Logistics Pipeline Control Center Manager, Pipeline Compliance Manager and Fleet Safety Director, group internal audit reporting to the board audit committee, and the disclosure committee

title: Group: HR roster by division
source_system: Group HR system (HR SaaS)
what_it_shows: 45,000 employees: Crude Oil Production about 26,000 (including about 140 production controllers and its own well servicing, roustabout and water handling crews), Power Generation about 2,200, Crude Logistics about 9,800 (including 18 pipeline controllers, about 3,900 drivers and about 300 commercial, dispatch and measurement staff), corporate shared services about 7,000. Employees work in Texas, New Mexico, Oklahoma and Florida. Termination events feed SYS-G1 identity governance. Open requisitions include 6 OT security engineering positions; no OT technician position is assigned to the Mid-Continent field sites

title: Group: FY2025 revenue by division
source_system: ERP general ledger; FY2025 Form 10-K segment note
what_it_shows: Revenue of about $18.0 billion: Crude Oil Production about $14.2 billion, Power Generation about $2.1 billion, Crude Logistics about $1.7 billion from third parties, plus about $0.9 billion of Crude Logistics intercompany revenue eliminated in consolidation

title: Group: contract register
source_system: Legal contract management system
what_it_shows: No federal contracts or subcontracts and no payment card acceptance agreement are recorded. Contracts include the intercompany transportation and data agreement between Production and Crude Logistics (2025); the gas purchase contract with the third-party gas processor and the Power Generation netback contract for residue gas from that processor; turbine OEM remote monitoring and tuning service agreements for Plants P1, P2 and P3; joint operating agreements with about 2,600 non-operating working interest owners; transportation contracts with about 85 third-party shippers and producers, which describe services, dispute windows and statement dates and state no security or availability commitments; the hydrocarbon accounting, payroll and telematics SaaS agreements, of which the hydrocarbon accounting and telematics agreements set no breach notice or cooperation terms; and the Mid-Continent legacy SCADA integrator contract inherited with the 2025-09-30 acquisition

title: Group: SYS-G1 authentication and sign-in policy export
source_system: Identity platform admin console
what_it_shows: 45,000 workforce identities with unique identifiers that are never reused. MFA is required for all workforce on SSO applications, including SYS-P3, SYS-P4, SYS-E3 and staff access to SYS-M3; IT administrators use phishing-resistant MFA. Accounts lock after repeated failed sign-ins; business accounts are disabled after 45 days of inactivity. Integrators and vendors sign in as named external identities before reaching PAM. Federated assertions are signed by SYS-G1

title: Group: SYS-G1 identity governance configuration and service account register
source_system: Identity governance console
what_it_shows: Joiner-mover-leaver workflows driven by HR events for all divisions; automated provisioning and disabling for business access to SYS-P3 and SYS-P4; quarterly certification campaigns for division applications and privileged roles, with access requests approved by role owners. The service account register lists the SYS-G6 historian connector account. SCADA local accounts are created from approved requests and carry the SYS-G1 identifier, and contractor SCADA accounts are tied to SYS-G1 identities

title: Group: PAM configuration, policy and session recordings, including the shared OT support jump servers
source_system: PAM console
what_it_shows: Privileged access to SCADA servers, OT DMZ hosts and cloud administration is granted just in time through PAM with phishing-resistant MFA and session recording; session recordings and administrator logs are forwarded to the SIEM and watched by the SOC OT desk; remote sessions use encrypted tunnels and the PAM gateway uses TLS. Five OT support jump servers in SYS-G1 are the PAM landing path for OT support staff and approved vendors of all three divisions. Vendor maintenance sessions for the FSPA run only through PAM; only PAM-elevated engineers can change SCADA servers

title: Group: OT DMZ standard, jump server and OT DMZ firewall rule exports
source_system: Firewall management console; OT security standards library
what_it_shows: The OT DMZ standard requires deny-by-default rules, no direct IT-to-OT paths, and jump server access only from privileged access workstations. Firewall rules permit the five shared jump servers to reach the Production, Power Generation and Crude Logistics OT DMZs and the Mid-Continent legacy SCADA (SYS-P5) network, and permit connections from the corporate virtual desktop pool to the jump servers. Rules at each of the three OT DMZs permit the SYS-G6 historian connector inbound to the historian broker. The Production OT DMZs at the IOC and BCC hold the historian broker, patch and antivirus relays and the PAM landing point; OT DMZ firewalls deny by default, allow by exception and fail closed; historian replica data otherwise leaves the Production OT DMZ outbound only. Plant and GCC rule sets record a reason for each rule

title: Group: SYS-G6 historian connector configuration and interface register
source_system: Data platform console; secret store; interface register
what_it_shows: One SYS-G6 service account pulls historian data from the historian brokers in all three divisions' OT DMZs, and its permissions on the brokers include write. Its secret is held in the secret store with 90-day rotation. The interface register documents the SYS-P3, SYS-P4 and SYS-G6 interfaces and the historian and alarm forwarding links from SYS-P5 to the IOC; no interconnection agreement is on file for the SYS-G6 connector or the SYS-P5 links. Data scientists hold read-only roles on curated historian data in the machine learning workspace, which has no network route to any OT DMZ

title: Group: SIEM data source inventory, OT sensor coverage map and detection rules
source_system: SIEM; OT monitoring console
what_it_shows: 24x7 SOC with an OT desk since 2025. Onboarded sources include SYS-G1 sign-ins, PAM sessions, cloud audit logs from providers A and B, EDR, OT DMZ firewalls, and SCADA server, historian and engineering workstation logs from the IOC and BCC, collected under the OT logging profile. Passive OT monitoring sensors feed the OT console from the Permian IOC, the BCC, the Pipeline Control Center and the Generation Control Center. The Mid-Continent legacy SCADA (SYS-P5) and the Florida control room SCADA application logs are not on the data source list. Use cases cover atypical sign-ins and PAM sessions and new engineering sessions to SCADA servers; correlation rules join OT sensor alerts with SYS-G1 sign-ins and EDR events; threat intelligence enriches OT alerts; flow alerts watch traffic at the OT DMZ. Logs are archived write-once (1 year online and 6 years archived for OT security events) and OT administrators cannot delete them

title: Group: SOC case records, OT playbook and exercise records, 2025 to Q1 2026
source_system: SOC case management system; playbook library
what_it_shows: Incidents are tracked in one case system with discovery dates and chain of custody, rated on the group severity scale and routed to the IOC shift lead and the division lead. The OT playbook names the IOC shift lead, the SCADA vendor and the carriers and covers OT DMZ isolation, manual operations, recovery and rebuild from known-good images; the IT forensic evidence procedure has no steps for capturing controller logic or HMI state. Quarterly technical playbook exercises run per division; the records include no cross-division exercise with the notification matrix. Incident response training records cover SOC staff, division liaisons and controller escalation

title: Group: EDR coverage report
source_system: EDR console
what_it_shows: EDR runs on all IT servers and workstations, cloud hosts, the jump servers, file servers, and the FSPA SCADA servers and engineering workstations. Container images are scanned at build. No SYS-P5 host appears in the console

title: Group: vulnerability scan, KEV tracking and patch reports, Q1 2026
source_system: Vulnerability scanner; OT monitoring console; KEV tracking sheet; patch records
what_it_shows: Business IT, cloud hosts and SYS-M3 hosts and images are scanned weekly, with configuration drift alerts. OT vulnerabilities on SCADA and OT DMZ servers are identified passively from sensor data and from vendor and CISA ICS advisories. The KEV tracking sheet lists open known exploited vulnerabilities on OT DMZ and SCADA servers with their open dates against a 30-day remediation target. OT patches are tested on the development SCADA system and applied quarterly; SCADA vendor updates are installed on SYS-P1 servers quarterly after that test; controller firmware is installed with no recorded check of vendor signatures or hashes

title: Group: SOC OT desk advisory log and sharing memberships
source_system: SOC OT desk records
what_it_shows: The OT desk logs CISA ICS advisories and vendor notices and assigns actions. The group receives E-ISAC sharing through the Power Generation membership and belongs to an oil and gas information sharing forum. The group vulnerability disclosure process routes vendor advisories to the OT desk

title: Group: business IT penetration test report, 2026-04
source_system: Independent penetration test report
what_it_shows: An independent penetration test of business IT and the cloud landing zones ran in 2026-04. The IT/OT boundary and the OT DMZs were outside its scope

title: Group: policy and standards library
source_system: Policy repository (intranet)
what_it_shows: Group policies POL-01 to POL-05 (2025 versions) aligned to CSF 2.0, with group procedures for awareness and training, assessment and authorization, configuration management, contingency planning, identification and authentication, incident response and risk assessment. Group standards: the OT DMZ standard, the OT reference architecture (OT DMZ, zones and conduits, defense in depth), the logging standard (1 year online and 6 years archived for OT security events), the OT logging profile, cloud guardrails and hardening guidance, and the group information security program plan. The library holds no AI standard

title: Group: policy register and division supplements
source_system: Policy repository; division supplement folders
what_it_shows: The policy register lists group policies and standards and no division supplement versions. The Production supplement adds the OT access standard (named SCADA accounts, vendor sessions only through PAM, field device credential rules), field logic change rules and OT role training. The Power Generation supplement v2026 was aligned on 2026-03-10 with the CIP-003-9 policy approval. The Crude Logistics supplement v2023 was last aligned in 2023-05 and names no owner; it allows a standing SCADA vendor VPN for support, uses a division 3-level incident severity scale, sets termination by the next business day, limits change management to field and display changes, names PHMSA and the National Response Center as its only notices, and does not address common control inheritance or AI use

title: Group: common control catalog and inheritance matrices
source_system: GRC tool
what_it_shows: The 2025 catalog lists 81 group common controls, each with a named provider (SYS-G1, SYS-G2, SYS-G3 and group functions). Inheritance matrices exist for Crude Oil Production (2025) and Power Generation (2025, mapped to the CIP-003-9 low impact plans). No Crude Logistics matrix was provided

title: Group: cloud account inventory, providers A and B
source_system: Cloud provider consoles; configuration database
what_it_shows: Provider A hosts the corporate landing zone and hub, SYS-G6, SYS-P4, SYS-P6, SYS-M3 and the SYS-E3 servers in one primary region; provider B hosts disaster recovery replicas and the immutable backup vault. Each division has its own accounts inside each landing zone, federated from SYS-G1, with IAM roles limited to its own accounts. SYS-P1, SYS-E1, SYS-E2 and SYS-M1 run on premises at their control centers and plants and are not in the cloud inventory. The configuration database records cloud services and the SCADA software and versions for SYS-P1

title: Group: landing-zone guardrail, hub network and firewall policy reports
source_system: Guardrail policy service; hub firewall management
what_it_shows: Mandatory policies on every division account (no public storage, approved regions only, encryption required, unapproved services blocked) with a compliance report; workloads hardened to the landing-zone baseline. Hub-and-spoke network with deny-by-default rules between division accounts and toward the WAN; the SYS-E3 spoke has no route to the GCC or plant OT networks. Provider DDoS protection on public endpoints, gateway rate limits, and a web application firewall in front of the shipper portal

title: Group: key management inventory and encryption settings
source_system: Key management service; storage and disk encryption reports
what_it_shows: Customer-managed keys per division account in the provider key services. Cloud storage is encrypted at rest by policy, including SYS-G6, the SYS-P4 workloads, SYS-P6 project storage and the SYS-M3 database; SYS-P3 data is encrypted at rest by the vendor; SCADA server disks are encrypted

title: Group: WAN design, TLS and IPsec settings, and external TLS scan, Q1 2026
source_system: Network management system; TLS scanner
what_it_shows: Private WAN links to control centers, plants and field offices use IPsec; business, cloud, portal and app traffic uses TLS; control traffic stays on each division's OT network and does not cross the WAN; field offices have cellular failover

title: Group: backup vault configuration, replication and restore records
source_system: Backup service (provider B vault)
what_it_shows: Daily backups of cloud workloads (including SYS-M3) and SCADA server images go to the provider B vault with immutability and a separate backup identity; replication reports show the vault as alternate storage in a second provider; restore records list quarterly test restores of SCADA server images from the vault; the SYS-M3 managed database has point-in-time recovery

title: Group: productivity suite admin export
source_system: Productivity suite admin console
what_it_shows: Email, files and chat for the 45,000 workforce users, with sign-in through SYS-G1 and MFA; email security filtering on inbound mail

One notification matrix, owned by the Group General Counsel, lists NERC E-ISAC and EOP-004 reports, PHMSA and EPA notices, the SEC materiality decision, state breach notices, and shipper and market notices; no exercise of the matrix is recorded, and it holds no shipper notice terms. Printed offline contact binders are kept at the control centers. Group legal keeps a 50-state breach notice summary; no notice template for Florida individuals or royalty owners is on file, and royalty owner mailing addresses have no yearly check

The FY2025 annual report's Item 106 disclosure describes the group program, OT security, the use of internal audit to assess common controls, board risk committee oversight and the Group CISO's reporting line

Group risk assessment procedure; 2025 group and division registers; supply chain risk records for SCADA, controller and integrator suppliers; division leads report monthly to the Group CISO

Annual code of conduct and POL-05 rules-of-behavior acknowledgments. OT security role training for Production controllers and automation technicians at hire and every 2 years; role training for SYS-M3 platform engineers; an awareness module for Crude Logistics drivers and terminal staff; quarterly plant security briefings at Power Generation

title: Group: HR procedures, screening, contractor and sanctions records
source_system: Group HR system
what_it_shows: Background checks before hire for controllers, automation staff, platform engineers, drivers and terminal staff, with driving record checks for drivers and terminal staff; identity proofing at hire; contractor register with sponsors; integrator and vendor staff sign the group OT access agreement and complete training before access; the exit checklist triggers same-day SYS-G1 disablement; group sanctions procedure and 2025 sanctions log

title: Group: accounts payable vendor master, supplier risk register and SCRM plan
source_system: ERP vendor master; third-party risk tool
what_it_shows: Tiered vendor program under the group supply chain risk management plan, which covers OT suppliers. The group OT security contract schedule has been required in new SCADA, controller and integrator contracts since 2025; contracts signed before 2025, including the Mid-Continent legacy SCADA integrator and 3 controller vendors, do not include it. SCADA, controller, accounting and carrier suppliers are ranked by criticality; the legacy integrator is not on the ranked list. The supplier assessment list records onboarding assessments of tier 1 OT suppliers and no assessment of the legacy integrator. Due diligence for new OT suppliers (questionnaire and architecture review), offboarding steps (access removal, return of data and programs), callback verification of vendor bank changes, and a receiving inspection procedure for controllers

title: Group: vendor SOC 2 Type 2 reports on file

what_it_shows: SOC 2 Type 2 reports are on file for cloud providers A and B (including physical security and media sanitization at provider facilities), the identity SaaS vendor, the SIEM vendor, the hydrocarbon accounting SaaS vendor, the bidding SaaS vendor and the telematics vendor, each with a review record; the hydrocarbon accounting report is reviewed each year

The 2026 strategy review covers the Mid-Continent acquisition and the SYS-P5 migration to SYS-P1 due 2027-09-30. The group integration checklist for acquisitions covers business systems only. The communications plan has group communications approve public statements

title: Crude Oil Production: well, facility and volume report
source_system: Production reporting; operations dashboards
owner: Production Vice President of Operations Technology
collected_by: Group GRC team with the Production security and compliance lead
what_it_shows: About 16,800 operated wells (11,200 producing, 4,300 water injection, 600 saltwater disposal, 700 shut-in), 410 central tank batteries, 95 associated gas compression stations and 38 water injection plants. About 520,000 barrels of oil per day gross operated: Permian Basin about 74%, Mid-Continent about 22% (including the fields acquired 2025-09-30, about 2,900 wells on SYS-P5), Florida Panhandle about 4%. About 1.4 million barrels of produced water per day are injected or disposed. Associated gas is sold at central facility outlets to a third-party gas processor. All wells and facilities are onshore

title: Crude Oil Production: SPCC plans, alarm list and spill procedure
source_system: HSE records; SCADA alarm configuration
collected_by: Group GRC team with the Production security and compliance lead
what_it_shows: About 250 of the 410 central tank batteries use the high-level sensor option of 40 CFR 112.9(c)(4)(iv), with alarms transmitted to the field SCADA; wells stop on loss of tank level signal. The plans do not describe actions when the alarm path to SCADA fails. The HSE spill procedure lists the National Response Center number and an on-call HSE coordinator and assumes control room phones and email; 2025 notice records are on file

title: Crude Oil Production: safety system design records and controller fail-safe settings
source_system: Engineering document system; controller configuration
collected_by: Group GRC team with the Production security and compliance lead
what_it_shows: Hardwired shutdowns for H2S, tank high level and compressor emergency shutdown act independent of SCADA at central facilities and compressor stations. Field controllers hold last state or go to a defined safe state on loss of communications, and rod pump controllers enforce minimum and maximum speeds locally. Portable H2S monitors are issued to field crews

title: Crude Oil Production: SYS-P1 account export, role matrix and console settings
source_system: SCADA administration console
owner: Production Vice President of Operations Technology
collected_by: Group GRC team with the Production security and compliance lead
what_it_shows: About 140 production controllers at the Permian IOC, the BCC and the Florida control room hold named local SCADA accounts tied to SYS-G1 identifiers; the Florida control room also has 2 shared HMI operator logins. Roles separate view-only, controller and engineer rights, and engineers who change logic cannot approve their own changes. SCADA servers lock after 5 failed sign-ins; controller console HMIs are exempt from lockout under a recorded exemption, with console physical access control. A monthly script flags SCADA accounts inactive for 60 days. Sign-in banners are set where the software allows. SCADA event logs record user, console, command, point and time; servers, historians and supporting field devices synchronize to OT time servers in the DMZ. Unused services and ports are disabled; USB ports are blocked on controller consoles, and removable media pass through scanning kiosks; application allowlisting runs on IOC and BCC HMIs

title: Crude Oil Production: OT asset inventory, baselines and unsupported component list
source_system: OT monitoring console (passive discovery); site survey records; baseline library
owner: Production Vice President of Operations Technology
collected_by: Group GRC team with the Production security and compliance lead
what_it_shows: About 38,000 field control devices (RTUs, PLCs, rod pump controllers, ESP variable speed drives, flow computers) and about 9,000 cellular modems; about 85% of field devices have model, firmware and address recorded. SYS-P5 devices are not in the inventory. The unsupported component list includes the 22 Florida control room HMIs and the SYS-P5 HMIs. Baselines exist for SCADA servers, HMIs, engineering workstations and each controller model; an asset lifecycle plan covers spares for controllers and servers

title: Crude Oil Production: field communications inventory and radio replacement plan
source_system: Network management system; radio license records
owner: Production Vice President of Operations Technology
collected_by: Group GRC team with the Production security and compliance lead
what_it_shows: Private LTE with SIM-based device authentication and encryption, with a redundant core at the IOC. Licensed radio links at about 30% of Permian sites carry legacy protocols with no encryption or device-level authentication; SCADA plausibility checks run on key values. About 9,000 cellular modems have web management interfaces. The replacement plan moves the licensed radio sites to private LTE by 2027-12-31. Capacity is monitored for SCADA servers, the LTE core and links

title: Crude Oil Production: OT change board records and program repository report

collected_by: Group GRC team with the Production security and compliance lead

The program repository holds PLC and RTU programs for about 60% of controller models, with a monthly logic comparison against the field for those models

title: Crude Oil Production: FSPA contingency plan, 2025 BCC failover test and recovery procedures

owner: Production Vice President of Operations Technology
collected_by: Group GRC team with the Production security and compliance lead

title: Crude Oil Production: Mid-Continent legacy SCADA (SYS-P5) network diagram, remote access and backup records
